rule: the admitted set: git-tracked per checkout, extensions c,h from the router's ONE table, admitted BY SPELLING the way the gate admits (a lowercase suffix test; the gate's bare-basename clause cannot fire for c,h), present on disk, ≤ 1 MiB

rulings.decorates: ONTOLOGICAL: attribute sites exist (attributeSites counted, split GNU attribute_specifier vs C23 attribute_declaration) and carry names, but an attribute is passive metadata — the compiler interprets its argument as a VALUE (`aligned(16)`, `format(printf,1,2)`, `alias("sym")`), never as a callable the declaration applies. THE CONTRACT (src/ast/types.ts, Decorates) is 'a decorator is APPLIED TO a declaration ... the runtime applies it while the declaration is created', so the positive test is an attribute whose argument IS AN INVOKED CALLABLE. C's one such attribute is `cleanup(fn)`/`gnu::cleanup(fn)`. FALSIFIER (three counters, all instrument-counted): (a) appliedCallableAttributeSites — any `cleanup`/`gnu::cleanup`/`__cleanup__` site, wherever the named function is declared, must be 0; (b) callableAttributeArguments — a call-shaped argument whose CALLEE names a CALLABLE this file declares (kind function/method/constructor) must be 0; (c) the near-miss class nonCallableDeclaredCallee, the four `alias(__MINGW64_STRINGIFY(__MINGW_IMP_SYMBOL(x)))` sites where the callee is a function-like macro and the declared name is published as a VARIABLE (kind variable) — a macro computing a compiler directive's argument at preprocessing time is not an application of anything. Measured 0 / 0 / 4-named-impostor over 20,824 files.
rulings.renders: ONTOLOGICAL: C has no component concept — no render-shaped node type exists in the served grammar (renderShapedNodes = 0 over the whole population, and the grammar's own node-type inventory carries no render/view/component production). The falsifier is the census itself: any render-shaped node in an admitted file would print as a sample and refute the ruling.
rulings.mixes_in: ONTOLOGICAL: C has no supertype chain — a struct's members are NAMED, never inherited or composed into a chain, and a struct is a supertype of nothing — so there is no construct a mixin could compose into (compositionShapedNodes = 0). The one textual near miss is the QUOTED INCLUDE INSIDE A STRUCT BODY (`struct X { #include "fields.h" };`), counted as quotedIncludeInsideStruct = 0 over the whole population, and it fails the contract's own positive test either way: the vocabulary's mixes_in composes the mixin's implementation into a SUPERTYPE CHAIN and no conformance is declared, while an included field block declares no supertype and no conformance — it is part_of's territory (the preprocessor splices the header's TEXT into the translation unit, the part sharing the unit's single scope). FALSIFIER: a construct that makes an included field block a DECLARED supertype of the including struct — a conformance the type system can name — would be the supertype-chain half the contract requires, and any non-zero quotedIncludeInsideStruct or compositionShapedNodes count in this census's output would name it.
